{{Distinguish|Synthetic population (biology)}}
'''Synthetic population''' is artificial population data that fits the distribution of people and their relevant characteristics living in a specified area as according to the demographics from [[census]] data.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Huynh |first1=N |last2=Namazi-Rad |first2=Mohammad-Reza |last3=Perez |first3=P. |last4=Berryman |first4=M. |last5=Chen |first5=Q. |last6=Barthelemy |first6=J. |title=Generating a synthetic population in support of agent-based modeling of transportation in Sydney |journal=Faculty of Engineering and Information Sciences - Papers: Part A |date=1 January 2013 |pages=1357–1363 |url=https://ro.uow.edu.au/eispapers/1737/}}</ref> Synthetic populations are often a basis for [[microsimulation]] or also [[agent based model]]s of population behavior.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Hörl |first1=Sebastian |last2=Balac |first2=Milos |title=Synthetic population and travel demand for Paris and Île-de-France based on open and publicly available data |journal=Transportation Research Part C |date=2021 |volume=130 |article-number=103291 |doi=10.1016/j.trc.2021.103291 |bibcode=2021TRPC..13003291H |url=https://hal.science/hal-03286361/ |language=en|hdl=20.500.11850/495494 |hdl-access=free }}</ref> The latter can be used for simulation of disease transmission,<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Xu |first1=Zhujing |last2=Glass |first2=Kathryn |last3=Lau |first3=Colleen L. |last4=Geard |first4=Nicholas |last5=Graves |first5=Patricia |last6=Clements |first6=Archie |title=A synthetic population for modelling the dynamics of infectious disease transmission in American Samoa |journal=Scientific Reports |date=2017 |volume=7 |issue=1 |page=16725 |doi=10.1038/s41598-017-17093-8  |doi-access=free|pmid=29196679 |pmc=5711879 |bibcode=2017NatSR...716725X |s2cid=256907125 |url=https://researchonline.jcu.edu.au/51831/ |language=en |issn=2045-2322}}</ref> traffic<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Mueller |first1=Kirill |last2=Axhausen |first2=Kay W. |title=Hierarchical IPF: Generating a synthetic population for Switzerland |journal=ERSA Conference Papers |date=September 2011 |url=https://ideas.repec.org/p/wiw/wiwrsa/ersa11p305.html}}</ref> and similar.

Synthetic population are initial sets of agents with detailed demographic and socioeconomic attributes, which allow execution of agent-based microsimulation.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Zhu |first1=Yi |last2=Ferreira |first2=Joseph |title=Synthetic Population Generation at Disaggregated Spatial Scales for Land Use and Transportation Microsimulation |journal= Transportation Research Record |date=January 2014 |volume=2429 |issue=1 |pages=168–177 |doi=10.3141/2429-18|s2cid=16819119 }}</ref> Due to privacy reasons and data limitations and restrict observability of entire real population. Therefore, the population synthesis procedure is applied, which expands a small data sample of population by using auxiliary data, to generate a synthetic population as close as possible to the real population in its characteristics. 

==Examples of application==

Chicago Social Interaction Model (''chiSIM'') is an agent-based simulation of individuals and locations in [[Chicago]] along with their daily behavior. The population is modeled as a set of heterogeneous, interacting, adaptive agents. These agents are the population of all the residents of Chicago.<ref>{{cite book |last1=Macal |first1=Charles M. |last2=Collier |first2=Nicholson T. |last3=Ozik |first3=Jonathan |last4=Tatara |first4=Eric R. |last5=Murphy |first5=John T. |title=2018 Winter Simulation Conference (WSC) |chapter=Chisim: An Agent-Based Simulation Model of Social Interactions in a Large Urban Area |date=December 2018 |pages=810–820 |doi=10.1109/WSC.2018.8632409 |isbn=978-1-5386-6572-5 |s2cid=59600666 }}</ref>

In 2023, World Data Lab created a synthetic population for [[New York City|New York]] using [[Microdata (statistics)|microdata]] and [[summary statistics]].<ref>{{cite news |title=Fighting poverty with synthetic data |url=https://www.brookings.edu/articles/fighting-poverty-with-synthetic-data/ |access-date=6 July 2023 |work=Brookings |date=2023}}</ref> It was used to calculate the poverty levels among the neighborhoods for targeted social programs.

A synthetic population for [[Germany]] was built and is marketed by [[Statista]] under the name ''SynthiePop''.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Statista |title=Synthetische Populationsdaten |url=https://de.statista.com/business/de/synthiepop |access-date=2026-07-09 |website=de.statista.com |language=de}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Lewanczik |first=Niklas |date=2026-01-20 |title=Synthetische Populationen: Einfaches Targeting per Knopfdruck |url=https://onlinemarketing.de/performance-marketing/synthetische-populationen-targeting-auf-knopfdruck |access-date=2026-07-09 |website=OnlineMarketing.de |language=de}}</ref> It was already applied together with the [[Federal Railway Authority|German Federal Railway Authority]] to study the local impact of cheaper public transport passes.<ref>{{Cite web |last=EBA, DZSF |date=2026 |title=Die Kosten des Pendelns und der Einfluss des Deutschlandtickets |url=https://www.dzsf.bund.de/SharedDocs/Downloads/DZSF/Veroeffentlichungen/Forschungsberichte/2026/ForBe_91_2026_Pendelkosten.pdf?__blob=publicationFile&amp;v=4}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=DZSF  -  Projekte - Die Kosten des Pendelns und der Einfluss des Deutschlandtickets |url=https://www.dzsf.bund.de/SharedDocs/Standardartikel/DZSF/Projekte/Projekt_183_Pendelkosten.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250520170208/https://www.dzsf.bund.de/SharedDocs/Standardartikel/DZSF/Projekte/Projekt_183_Pendelkosten.html |archive-date=2025-05-20 |access-date=2026-07-09 |website=www.dzsf.bund.de |language=de}}</ref>

In [[Switzerland]], the [[Federal Office for Spatial Development|Swiss Federal Office for Spatial Development]] and the [[Swiss Federal Railways]] created a synthetic population to better plan traffic.<ref>{{Cite web |last=ARE, SBB |date=2022 |title=Synthetische Population 2022 |url=https://www.are.admin.ch/dam/de/sd-web/WTmt7B7TDBf2/Schlussbericht_Synpop2022_Publikation.pdf}}</ref>
